issues.legal_issue: The residuary rule for recovering excise duty was within the rule-making authority conferred by the enabling law.
material_facts: The Department demanded excise duty from a manufacturer after it resumed manufacturing steel, and the demand was confirmed by the competent authority.
The High Court quashed the demand on the basis that the residuary rule did not apply where there had been no prior levy.
The enabling law authorized rules to carry out its purposes, and its excise-duty provisions addressed both levy and collection.
issues.conclusion: The residuary rule, as it stood at the relevant time, was valid and not ultra vires the rule-making power.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 37(1) of the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944, the Central Government could make rules to carry out the purposes of the Act; the matters listed in Section 37(2) were not exhaustive. Section 3 addressed levy and collection of excise duty, so a rule providing a residual mechanism for collection was within that authority. The Court agreed with Kerala Polythene v. Superintendent, Central Excise; relied on Chhotabhai Jethabhai Patel v. Union of India; and distinguished Citadel Fine Pharmaceuticals v. District Revenue Officer and M/s. Agarwal Brothers v. Union of India. It also applied the principle in State of Kerala v. K.M. Charia Abdullah & Co. that delegated legislation may be challenged if the enabling power is exceeded or wrongfully exercised.

predicates.delegated_rule_validity_appeal: A party brings an appeal in which the validity of a delegated rule is at issue.
predicates.enabling_law_authorizes_levy_and_collect: The enabling law authorizes rules concerning the levy and collection of the relevant duty.
predicates.rule_furthers_enabling_law_purposes: The challenged rule provides a mechanism that carries out the purposes of the enabling law.

issues.definition: When a validity appeal concerns a rule made under authority covering levy and collection, and the rule carries out the enabling law’s purposes, the rule is valid.

issues.legal_issue: The residuary recovery rule could support a demand for excise duty even when no prior assessment had been made, provided no specific collection procedure applied.
material_facts: The manufacturer resumed steel production after taking back possession of its mill and applied for a licence.
The Department later demanded duty on the manufactured steel, and the demand was confirmed by the competent authority.
The High Court held that the residuary rule did not apply because there had been no prior levy of duty.
The rules contained specific collection procedures for some situations, while the residuary rule applied where no specific provision covered collection of the duty or deficiency.
issues.conclusion: The residuary rule applied only where no specific provision in the rules provided for collection; the absence of any prior assessment did not itself prevent recovery under that rule. The Court set aside the High Court’s order and remanded the matter, leaving other grounds of challenge open.
issues.legal_principle: The residuary rule was a collection mechanism applying when the rules made no specific provision for collecting the duty or deficiency. Under the distinction explained in N.B. Sanjana v. Elphinstone Spinning and Weaving Mills Company Ltd., Assistant Collector v. National Tobacco Co. Ltd., and D.R. Kohli v. Atul Products Ltd., the residuary provision did not apply where a specific collection rule governed, but could apply to an otherwise uncovered case, including one in which no assessment had been made. The rule did not itself create a charge beyond the duty authorized by the enabling law.

rule.if: excise_duty_recovery_proceeding and duty_or_deficiency_is_recoverable_under_enabling_law and no_prior_assessment and no_specific_collection_procedure

predicates.excise_duty_recovery_proceeding: The proceeding concerns recovery of excise duty or a deficiency in that duty.
predicates.duty_or_deficiency_is_recoverable_under_: The duty or deficiency sought is recoverable under the enabling law.
predicates.no_prior_assessment: No assessment of the duty was made before the recovery demand.
predicates.no_specific_collection_procedure: No specific procedure in the applicable rules provides for collection of the duty or deficiency.

issues.definition: In an excise-duty recovery proceeding, when the duty is recoverable, no prior assessment exists, and no specific collection procedure applies, the residuary recovery rule is available.
